sources.title: Flink: Fix microsecond truncation for timestamps in arrays and maps (#18001)
claims: PR merged into main at the recorded event_date; no release inclusion was verified.
StructRowData timestamp conversion now preserves microseconds before splitting epoch milliseconds and nano-of-millisecond.
Patch updates Flink 1.20, 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 source paths; the added array regression includes timestamps before and after the Unix epoch.
合并源码以 Math.floorDiv(micros, 1000L) 和 Math.floorMod(micros, 1000L) * 1000 拆分；epoch 前 1 微秒为正文明确标注的算术推演。
sources.access_notes: Read official PR body and files through GitHub REST API; web PR page also accessible. Exact timestamp is pull request merged_at, not search closed_at or crawl time. Upstream tests were not rerun.

sources.title: Enable Iceberg Parquet page skipping with column indexes (#30971)
claims: PR merged into master; milestone field is 484, but actual release inclusion was not verified.
Iceberg reader gains parquet_use_column_index and receives a Parquet predicate, enabling page skipping for already indexed files.
PR states Trino Iceberg writer does not yet emit page indexes; tests cover deletion-related and row-position correctness. No benchmark speedup is claimed.
PR 正文直接给出 SET SESSION iceberg.parquet_use_column_index = false；文章限定 catalog 名为 iceberg。
sources.access_notes: Read full official PR body and relevant production/test diffs via GitHub API; web PR page accessible. References to #30976 were treated as dependencies described by this PR, not independently audited changes.

sources.title: feat(core): Support schema management over REST in RESTCatalog (#9673)
claims: PR merged into master; release not verified.
Actual scope is display-only schema history: load LATEST/EARLIEST/schema ID and list full TableSchema objects in descending schema ID order with pagination.
Existing getTable, alterTable and rollbackSchema operations keep their prior implementation; the patch adds compatibility tests for a server without the new endpoints.
sources.access_notes: Read full PR body, new REST GET implementation and test-file inventory through official GitHub API. Title alone overstates scope; claims follow the body and implementation. Did not execute tests.

claims: PR merged into master inside the window; creation was before the window and was not used as the event.

hoodie.vector.columns metadata preserves vector identity; ordinary arrays retain their prior representation. Release inclusion was not verified.

sources.title: feat(flink): support vector columns in Lance reader (#19842)

Scope excludes INT8/nested vectors and Lance schema evolution; PR includes file round-trip and COW/MOR upsert/compaction test coverage.

sources.title: [Kernel] Fix kernel corrupt checkpoint bug (#7221)
claims: PR merged into master at event_date; creation in July is background, not this week's event. Release inclusion was not verified.
Input iterator failure could cause resource close to flush, footer and publish an incomplete Parquet file; patch adds abort state for failed output.
Implementation covers staged temp/rename and abortable streams. PositionOutputStream documentation explicitly limits non-abortable streams writing directly to the destination.

sources.title: Parquet Page Index: Layout to Support Page Skipping
claims: Page index is optional ColumnChunk metadata; ColumnIndex locates candidate pages by values, and OffsetIndex maps row indexes to corresponding pages in other columns.
Page index separates page-level metadata so selective scans need not access every data page header before deciding which pages to skip.
Used only as format background; the three-page example is an author-created hypothetical layout, not a benchmark or new feature announcement.
sources.access_notes: Read official documentation body. The page footer records a website search-related modification on 2026-02-24; it is not treated as a feature release date. No claim that Page Index originated or changed during this weekly window.

sources.title: FoundationDB #13866: RangeDigest
claims: Merged to main; commit c3787dfbddee2e8afc670ba52bf8b7bf20d6fab0.
Storage-server-side SHA-256 leaf hashes summed modulo 2^256 give partition-independent content fingerprints.
Requires stopped writes and moving_data=0; not adversarial collision-resistant and not an online pinned-snapshot audit.
No released-version evidence established.
The additive combine is associative and commutative but requires every key-value to be counted exactly once.
Rate limiting and batching reuse existing audit controls; server-side hashing still scans the data.
sources.access_notes: Read live GitHub REST pull detail and files endpoint, including design/range-digest.md. Browser fetch of PR page returned cache miss. No benchmark reproduced; no speedup ratio used.

claims: Merged to main; commit 5f250030ec437d6c676355e7a99f92b8ec480747.
Checks full edge identity and affected rows, retrying when stale SQL directory entries have been replaced.
PR helper tests cover stale-identity, ABA and rollback; PR explicitly does not claim concurrent public API end-to-end testing.
Duplicate-name handling is separate PR #7526; not claimed as part of this PR.
SQL helper matches inode, type and optional edge row ID, with affected-row checks; conceptual timeline in article is derived from PR description, not a reproduced concurrent test.

sources.title: JuiceFS #7500: abandoned fetch must not turn failure into success
claims: Merged to main; commit 0e5cb0c8a74f75553af5b51050925dbd7332772e.
Late async callback could overwrite named return error after timeout.
Separate GET result state is accepted only after successful WithTimeout; load and loadRange changed.
This does not prove all timeout/buffer-lifetime races fixed.

The named-return corruption window is during return/defer before final return; no claim that an already-delivered return value changes retroactively. Article timing example is a mechanism illustration, not a reproduced trace.

sources.title: WriteGuards: Distributed Storage Support for Strongly Consistent Caches
claims: Official conference proceedings cover confirms July 13–15 2026; presentation BibTeX month jul.
Range-based guards checked by storage reject writes from previous cache owners.
Read motivation and core Sections 4–6; implementation uses TiDB and coordinated ownership; not a drop-in TTL mechanism.
Core Section 6.2 constrains SetGuard to start and complete within one ownership interval, non-overlapping calls for a key, and fresh unique values including retries.
A data OCC version check can still admit a previous owner write when the new owner has only read and cached an unchanged version.
sources.access_notes: Opened official presentation, PDF and relevant sections; did not reproduce performance results or perform exhaustive full-paper evaluation.
